oneTimers: Restructuring and other charge of $622M in Q2 2024, including $583M of employee termination expenses from restructuring actions initiated and substantially completed in the quarter to reduce costs and improve efficiency (Form 10-Q Note 13) — there was no such charge a year ago.
otherDetail: Interest income of $348M and $20M of other income, less $86M of interest expense — a net +$282M below operating profit.

takeaways.text: Energy generation and storage revenue doubled to $3,014M as Tesla deployed a record 9.4 GWh of storage in the quarter, up 158% from a year ago on higher Megapack deployments.
takeaways.title: Energy storage hit a record

takeaways.text: Automotive revenue fell 7% to $19,878M as lower average selling prices and 5% fewer deliveries outweighed a record $890M in regulatory credits, up from $282M a year ago.
takeaways.title: Car revenue fell despite record credits

takeaways.text: A $622M restructuring and other charge helped push operating income down 33% to $1,605M and narrowed the operating margin to 6.3% from 9.6% a year ago; $583M of the charge was employee termination expenses.
takeaways.title: Restructuring charge cut into profit

verdict: Tesla's revenue rose just 2% to $25.5B as a record energy-storage quarter and record regulatory credits offset lower car prices and fewer deliveries, while a $622M restructuring charge cut operating profit by a third.
